extracted.intended_audience: applicants for TN classification (USMCA), employers, and immigration practitioners (including those handling F, J, M SEVIS fee matters)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and standards governing TN (USMCA) professional classification (admission, documentation, extensions, readmission, employer changes, dependents, strikes, habitual residence rules) and SEVIS fee obligations for F, J, and M nonimmigrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary entry demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish that the alien's entry will be temporary, the alien must demonstrate to the satisfaction of the inspecting immigration officer that his or her work assignment in the United States will end at a predictable time and that he or she will depart upon completion of the assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: USMCA Appendix 2 professions and minimum qualification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the USMCA, an applicant seeking admission under this section shall demonstrate business activity at a professional level in one of the professions set forth in Appendix 2 to Annex 16-A of Chapter 16. The professions in Appendix 2 to Annex 16-A and the minimum requirements for qualification for each are as follows:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix lists numerous professions (Accountant; Architect; Computer Systems Analyst; Disaster Relief Insurance Claims Adjuster; Economist; Engineer; Forester; Graphic Designer; Hotel Manager; Industrial Designer; Interior Designer; Land Surveyor; Landscape Architect; Lawyer; Librarian; Management Consultant; Mathematician/Statistician; Range Manager/Range Conservationist; Research Assistant (post-secondary institution); Scientific Technician/Technologist; Social Worker; Sylviculturist; Technical Publications Writer; Urban Planner; Vocational Counselor; and many medical, allied, scientist, and teacher professions) with the specified minimum educational degrees, licenses, or combinations of post-secondary credentials and experience (e.g., baccalaureate/licenciatura degree; state/provincial license; post-secondary diploma/certificate plus three years experience; or specified professional credentials). The Appendix items should be read for the exact listed profession-by-profession qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'state/provincial license' and similar license terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The terms 'state/provincial license' and 'state/provincial/federal license' mean any document issued by a state, provincial, or federal government, as the case may be, or under its authority, but not by a local government, that permits a person to engage in a regulated activity or profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Post-Secondary Diploma'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Post-Secondary Diploma' means a credential issued, on completion of two or more years of postsecondary education, by an accredited academic institution in Canada or the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Post-Secondary Certificate'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Post-Secondary Certificate' means a certificate issued, on completion of two or more years of postsecondary education at an academic institution, by the federal government of Mexico or a state government in Mexico, an academic institution recognized by the federal government or a state government, or an academic institution created by federal or state law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematician includes Actuary (professional recognition requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'Mathematician' includes the profession of Actuary. An Actuary must satisfy the necessary requirements to be recognized as an actuary by a professional actuarial association or society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'professional actuarial association or society' means such an association or society operating in the territory of at least one of the Parties (Canada, Mexico, United States).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Technician/Technologist qualification standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Possession of (a) theoretical knowledge of any of the following disciplines: agricultural sciences, astronomy, biology, chemistry, engineering, forestry, geology, geophysics, meteorology, or physics; and (b) the ability to solve practical problems in any of those disciplines, or the ability to apply principles of any of those disciplines to basic or applied research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the professional-level qualification for the 'Scientific Technician/Technologist' Appendix category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biologist includes Plant Pathologist
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'Biologist' includes the profession of Plant Pathologist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission procedures for citizens of Mexico (TN)
rubrics_metrics.description: A citizen of Mexico who seeks temporary entry as a business person to engage in business activities at a professional level may be admitted to the United States in accordance with USMCA upon presentation of a valid passport and valid TN nonimmigrant visa at a U.S. Class A port-of-entry, an airport handling international traffic, or a pre-clearance/pre-flight station.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission procedures for citizens of Canada (TN)
rubrics_metrics.description: A citizen of Canada seeking temporary entry as a business person to engage in business activities at a professional level shall make application for admission with a Department officer at a U.S. Class A port-of-entry, at an airport handling international traffic, or at a pre-clearance/pre-flight station.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation required for TN application (proof and employer support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon application for a visa or, for Canadian citizens, admission at a port-of-entry, an applicant shall present: (i) proof of citizenship; and (ii) documentation demonstrating engagement in business activities at a professional level and demonstrating professional qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation may include a letter from the prospective U.S. employer(s) or the foreign employer, supported by diplomas, degrees, or professional memberships. Degrees from institutions outside Canada/Mexico/US must be accompanied by an evaluation by a reliable credentials evaluation service. Documentation shall fully affirm: (A) the profession under Appendix 2; (B) a description of professional activities including brief summary of daily duties if appropriate; (C) anticipated length of stay; (D) educational qualifications/credentials demonstrating professional level status; and (E) arrangements for remuneration.

rubrics_metrics.name: TN admission confirmation, classification, and fee requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A citizen of Canada or Mexico who qualifies shall be provided confirming documentation and admitted under classification symbol TN for a period not to exceed three years; the document shall bear the legend 'multiple entry.' The fee prescribed under 8 CFR 103.7(b)(1) shall be remitted by Canadian citizens upon admission pursuant to USMCA; upon remittance, the TN applicant shall be provided a DHS-issued receipt on the appropriate form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readmission with unexpired Form I-94
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien may be readmitted to the United States in TN classification for the remainder of the authorized period on Form I-94, without presentation of the employer letter or supporting documentation and without the prescribed fee, provided the original intended professional activities and employer(s) have not changed, and the Form I-94 has not expired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readmission without valid I-94 (alternate evidence requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the alien seeking readmission is no longer in possession of a valid, unexpired Form I-94 but the initial period has not lapsed, a new Form I-94 may be issued for the remaining validity and the alien can be readmitted in TN status if alternate evidence is presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Canadian citizens, alternate evidence may include a fee receipt for admission as TN or a previous admission stamp in passport and a confirming employer letter. For Mexican citizens, alternate evidence shall consist of presentation of a valid unexpired TN visa and evidence of a previous admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of stay — filing and eligibility conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. employer of a Canadian or Mexican citizen currently maintaining valid TN status may request an extension of stay by filing the appropriate form with the fee per 8 CFR 106.2, in accordance with form instructions with USCIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: (i) extension must be requested by filing appropriate form with fee; (ii) beneficiary must be physically present in the U.S. at time of filing; if required to leave while petition pending, petitioner may request USCIS notify the consular office or port-of-entry of approval; (iii) extension may be approved for a maximum period of three years; (iv) there is no specific limit on total period in TN status provided the alien continues TN activities and properly maintains status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readmission at border for a new three-year period
rubrics_metrics.description: A citizen previously admitted in TN status who has not violated status may apply at a DHS-designated port-of-entry, prior to expiration, for a new three-year period of admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must be supported by a new letter from the U.S. employer or foreign employer (for Canadians providing prearranged services) that meets requirements of paragraph (d), together with the appropriate filing fee per 8 CFR 106.2. Citizens of Mexico must present valid passport and valid unexpired TN visa when applying for readmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change or addition of U.S. employers — filing & restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A TN nonimmigrant who seeks to change or add a U.S. employer during the period of admission must have the new employer file Form I-129 with appropriate supporting documentation, including a letter describing the services to be performed, the time needed, and terms of remuneration. Employment with a different or additional employer is not authorized prior to Department approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, the applicant may apply for readmission at the border presenting documentation that meets paragraph (d) requirements. Fee remittance rules apply for Canadians per 8 CFR 106.2. Transfers to another location by same U.S. employer to perform same services (e.g., branch/office) require no action; transfers to a separately incorporated subsidiary or affiliate require compliance with the change/add employer filing/readmission provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spouse and unmarried minor children (TD) — admission and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The spouse or unmarried minor children of a TN nonimmigrant, if otherwise admissible, may be admitted, readmitted, or granted change/extension for the same period as the TN. They shall be classified as TD nonimmigrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements and rules: (1) Request for change or extension to TD requires appropriate form, fees, and evidence of principal's TN status; (2) TD dependents required to present valid unexpired TD visa unless exempt under 8 CFR 212.1; (3) confirming documentation issued to TD bear 'multiple entry' legend and there is no fee required for admission of spouse/children; (4) TD dependents shall not accept employment unless otherwise authorized under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of a strike or labor dispute on TN admissions and status
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Secretary of Labor certifies or informs USCIS that a strike or labor dispute involving a work stoppage is in progress and the temporary entry of a TN nonimmigrant may adversely affect settlement or employment of persons involved, the U.S. may refuse to issue an immigration document authorizing entry or employment of such an alien.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the alien has already commenced employment and is participating in a strike/work stoppage: (i) the alien remains subject to all Act provisions and TN regulations; (ii) status and authorized stay are not modified or extended by participation; (iii) participation in a strike/work stoppage will not constitute a ground for removal by itself, but violations of status or overstaying remain removable. If the strike/labor dispute is not certified or USCIS is not informed, the Director shall not deny a petition or entry based on such a non-certified strike.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitual resident — definitions (FAS/territories/compacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: 'Compacts' refers to the agreements of free association between the U.S. and the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia, and Palau. 'Freely associated states (FAS)' names those parts. 'Territories and possessions of the United States' means all territories and possessions to which the Act applies (e.g., Guam, Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands, Northern Mariana Islands), excluding American Samoa while Act does not apply to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitual resident — who qualifies and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'habitual resident' means a citizen of the FAS who has been admitted pursuant to section 141(a) of the Compacts and who occupies a habitual residence (place of general abode or principal actual dwelling place of continuing/lasting nature). The term does not apply to persons with cumulative physical presence under 365 days, dependents of resident representatives, or persons who entered for full-time studies as long as they maintain that status. It also does not apply where presence is based on other authority (e.g., armed forces members, persons lawfully admitted for permanent residence, or nonimmigrants with other authority).

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitual resident — dependent and principal habitual resident definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Dependent' means a citizen of the FAS who is a habitual resident, resides with a principal habitual resident, relies financially on that principal, and is parent/spouse/unmarried child under 21 (or parent/child of spouse). 'Principal habitual resident' means a habitual resident with whom dependents reside and on whom they rely for financial support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitual resident — 'self-supporting' standard
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Self-supporting' means: (i) having a lawful occupation of current and continuing nature that provides 40 hours of gainful employment each week (with part-time students receiving three hours toward the 40-hour requirement per credit-hour), or (ii) if unable to meet 40-hour requirement, having lawfully derived funds that meet or exceed 100% of the official poverty guidelines for Hawaii for a family unit of appropriate size as published by HHS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitual resident — receipt of unauthorized public benefits definition
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Receipt of unauthorized public benefits' means acceptance of public benefits by fraud or willful misrepresentation in violation of sections 401 or 411 of the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996, as amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitual resident — presumption of habitual residence on arrival
rubrics_metrics.description: An arriving FAS citizen will be subject to the rebuttable presumption of being a habitual resident if the Service has reason to believe the citizen was previously admitted more than one year ago and either failed to turn in Form I-94 when previously departing or failed to apply for a replacement Form I-94.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitual resident — rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Habitual residents have the right to enter, reside, study, and work in the United States, its territories or possessions, in nonimmigrant status without regard to the requirements of sections 212(a)(5)(A) and 212(a)(7)(A) and (B) of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitual resident — limitations and grounds for removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-dependent habitual residents who are not self-supporting for over 60 consecutive days (except for lawful strikes), who have received unauthorized public benefits by fraud or willful misrepresentation, or who are subject to removal under section 237 of the Act (or other provisions) are removable. Dependents are removable if the principal habitual resident becomes removable unless they establish dependency on another habitual resident or become self-supporting, or if the dependent individually receives unauthorized public benefits by fraud or misrepresentation, or is otherwise removable under section 237 or other provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS fee — applicability and amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliens in the categories below are required to submit payment in the specified amounts to SEVP in advance of obtaining F, J, or M status: (1) F-1 or F-3 applicants to enroll at an SEVP-certified school: $350; (2) J-1 applicants to commence participation in a Department of State-designated exchange visitor program: $220 (with reduced fees for certain exchange categories); (3) M-1 or M-3 applicants to enroll at an SEVP-certified vocational institution: $350.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS fee — aliens not subject to fee
rubrics_metrics.description: No SEVIS fee is required for: (1) a J-1 exchange visitor coming as participant in a Federal government-sponsored exchange program identified by program identifiers G-1, G-2, G-3, or G-7; (2) dependents of F, M, or J nonimmigrants (dependents do not pay separate fee though principal must pay when required).

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS — special fee for certain J-1 categories
rubrics_metrics.description: A J-1 exchange visitor coming as an au pair, camp counselor, or participant in a summer work/travel program is subject to a fee of $35.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS fee — timing for payment
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien subject to payment must remit the fee directly to DHS as follows: (1) those seeking F-1, F-3, J-1, M-1, or M-3 visas from consular officer abroad for initial attendance must pay before visa issuance; (2) visa-exempt aliens under 212(d)(4) must pay before applying for admission at port-of-entry to begin study/participation; (3) nonimmigrant aliens in U.S. seeking change of status to F/J/M must pay before change is granted (except as provided in paragraph (e)(4)); (4) J-1 changing program category in U.S. must pay fee associated with new category prior to grant; (5) J-1 initially granted J-1 in federal-sponsored program transferring to non-federal program must pay new program fee prior to completing transfer; (6) J-1 applying for reinstatement after substantive violation or out of program >120 but <270 days must pay a new fee prior to reinstatement; (7) F/M applying for reinstatement after violation and out of status past certain deadlines must pay new fee prior to return to valid status; (8) F/M nonimmigrant absent >5 months seeking to reenter for further study in same course generally must pay new fee prior to being granted student status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See specific subparagraphs for detailed exceptions and interplays with program transfer/reinstatement rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS fee — circumstances where no new fee required
rubrics_metrics.description: No new SEVIS fee is required in certain circumstances: (1) extension of stay, transfer, or optional practical training for students (listed 8 CFR references); (2) extension of program or transfer for exchange visitors; (3) visa issuance for continuation of study if fee previously paid and not otherwise required per other provisions; (4) certain changes in student classification (no fee for F-1 <-> F-3 or M-1 <-> M-3; DHS may waive fee for changes between F and M due solely to institutional reclassification); (5) re-application within 12 months after initial consular denial when fee was fully paid; (6) re-application following denial of a change of status if motion to reopen is granted within 12 months of initial denial and fee was fully paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS fee — procedures for payment
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien subject to payment may pay the fee by any procedure approved by DHS, including: (i) submission of Form I-901 by mail with check/money order/foreign draft payable in U.S. currency; (ii) electronic submission of Form I-901 using a credit card or other DHS-accepted electronic payment; or (iii) a designated payment service and receipt mechanism approved and set forth in future DHS guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS fee — receipts and proof of payment
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will provide a receipt for each fee payment until DHS issues Federal Register notice that paper receipts are unnecessary. Additional provisions: (i) DHS will provide expedited delivery of receipt upon request and additional fee; (ii) If payment made electronically, both DHS and Dept. of State will accept a properly printed electronic receipt in lieu of DHS-generated receipt; (iii) If paid through approved payment service, DHS and Dept. of State will accept receipt issued by that service in lieu of DHS-generated receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS fee — electronic record of payment
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will maintain an electronic record of payment for the alien as verification. If DHS records indicate fee paid, an alien who lost or did not receive a paper receipt will not be denied an immigration benefit, including visa issuance or admission, solely because of failure to present a paper receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS fee — third-party payments
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS will accept payment of the required fee for an alien from a certified school or a designated exchange visitor program sponsor, or from another source, in accordance with procedures approved by DHS.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEVIS fee — failure to pay is grounds for denial
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure to pay the required fee is grounds for denial of F, M, or J nonimmigrant status or status-related benefits.
